column1: # The one-line description under each tier header. Source of truth — all six filled.

column2: The programs the data sets clearly apart at the top. Each has hung banners across multiple eras, on sustained excellence rather than one run.
Just outside the inner circle. Their histories carry too much weight to ignore, and the numbers place them firmly in the tier right below the top.

The next tier, where the path to the top is less defined. Each has the history and the March résumé to make a run at blue-blood status, but needs more decades of sustained success — or a truly dominant era — to close the gap.
Programs the whole country knows, with real Final Four history. The band runs from genuine current risers to powers coasting on an era two or three decades back.
Recognisable names and real tournament pedigrees, but a clear class break below the powers. Also where newer high-major programs still accruing the cumulative totals land.
Everyone else — mostly one-bid leagues, regional followings and thin résumés, plus the young Division I programs whose ceilings haven’t been tested by the counting stats.
